On every negative cell g has no open-cell zero. Harmonic zero spacing pi/mu gives phi<pi; separate next-zero and previous-zero arguments cover the left and right Dirichlet endpoint cells and exclude equality.

On a positive cell choose f>0. Crossing order gives g(0)=f(0), g(theta)=-f(theta), while inward transversality gives S_s(0)>0>S_s(theta). Combining these strict inequalities with |y|>|f_s| yields y(0)<0 and y(theta)<0.

For the continuous high-state angle alpha=arg(g,y), alpha_s=-mu. Exact one-zero allocation places the terminal lift in (-3pi/2,-pi/2); its quadrant-III signs select (-pi,-pi/2), excluding the pi<phi<2pi branch and giving phi<pi.
Positive cell length and mu>1 then give 0<theta<phi=mu theta<pi for all 2n+1 cells.

ordered_step_reconstruction: Fixed-time q differentiation gives eta_U''+rho eta_U=-rho_q U and eta_V''+mu^2rho eta_V=-mu^2rho_q V. Direct Wronskian integration with common terminal positions gives p eta_U=int rho_q U^2 and r eta_V=mu^2 int rho_q V^2, with the displayed signs.

Differentiating rho=(R+1)/2+sigma(R-1)sign(S)/2 gives rho_q=sigma(R-1)delta(S)S_q. Since U^2=mu^2V^2 on the support, p eta_U=r eta_V and p eta_U=sigma(R-1)J. The accepted endpoint identity then yields sign(partial_q A_n)=-sigma sign(J).

Retarded variation of constants gives eta_U=-int G_U rho_q U and eta_V=V/q-mu^2 int G_V rho_q V. Substitution at ordered events and mu V_i=epsilon_i U_i yields the strictly lower-triangular system x_i=-2mu^2V_i^2/q+sigma(R-1)sum_(j<i)M_ij x_j/abs(d_j), with M_ij=2U_iU_j[-G_U+mu^2epsilon_i epsilon_jG_V], and J=sum U_i^2x_i/abs(d_i).
At R=1+epsilon and mu_0=(n+1)/n, scalar zero-time differentiation independently gives T_U,epsilon=-int chi_sigma a and T_V,epsilon=-int chi_sigma b. Thus F_+=int_(a>q^2b)(b-a)<0 and F_-=-F_+.

Distributional differentiation of the moving switching domain gives F_+'=sum(-2qb)(b-a)/abs(S_0') at a=q^2b, namely C_n=2q(q^2-1)sum b(t_j)^2/abs(S_0'(t_j))>0; F_-'=-C_n. Simplicity and no common interior zero make every term finite and positive.

Because A_n(mu,q,0)=n pi-(n+1)pi/mu has positive mu derivative and zero q and mixed q-mu derivatives at the base, the implicit common-terminal sheet exists locally and fixed-mu partial_q A_n=sigma epsilon C_n(q)+O(epsilon^2), uniformly on a compact q-neighborhood.

At equal norm q=mu_0 is a simple root, so the complete root persists locally. Constant-contrast event differentiation gives alternating, not common, displacement signs. Arbitrary finite-contrast J<0 and global one-root order remain open.
